prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, in which heterobifunctional molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to turn binding of a chosen protein into its removal

statement.case_for: I keep B007 as a single-part prize, and the first-round exchange has strengthened it. Five of eight members now include it, and the shared reasons are scientific: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex whose cooperativity can be measured and tuned, the principle has been reproduced across many E3 ligases and laboratories, and the outcome (disappearance of the target) is a different mechanism from inhibition. That is the test I apply as a physicist: a clear principle, quantitative evidence, and generative potential, since it reaches targets without a classical binding pocket. On attribution, the chair's question separates the original discovery from refinement. The induced-proximity concept and its first demonstration belong to Crews and Deshaies (2001). Ciulli supplied the structural and thermodynamic account of cooperativity and the VHL ligand chemistry that turned the concept into a rational design discipline. A citation worded around induced-proximity degradation by heterobifunctional molecules is defensible, can be explained in a sentence, and stays within three names. I would not stretch it to claim the cereblon glue strand as part of the credited discovery.
statement.case_against: Two weaknesses remain. First, cereblon glues (Handa, Ito, with Gray and Sakamoto) are a partly separate history, and a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli prize will be read as passing over them; I accept that cost rather than blur two stories, and the citation should say plainly that it concerns heterobifunctional degraders. Second, no degrader is yet an approved drug, and I cannot verify the late-stage trial status from the materials I may read. I regard this as a timing risk, not a scientific defect, because the principle is independently confirmed. If the expert report shows the principle to be less settled than the committee assumes, B029 is the safer, mature fallback.

responses.point: Aili proposes Crews, Ciulli and Handa, would accept Deshaies over Handa, and asks that the slate cover both the PROTAC and the cereblon glue strands honestly.
responses.response: I move toward your flexibility but not to your slate. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type drugs, a real mechanistic discovery about an existing drug. The design principle that lets chemists build a degrader for a chosen target started with Crews and Deshaies. Dropping Deshaies would leave the 2001 concept without a co-originator, and no round-1 argument for Handa rests on priority of the modality. I therefore take your fallback, Deshaies over Handa, and I support wording that does not suggest the glue branch is unimportant. If you can show that Handa's work was itself the design of a new modality and not an explanation of a known drug, I would reopen the third seat.

responses.point: Chabes proposes a two-part prize, base editing (Liu alone) and PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies), to cover two distinct achievements within the cap, and treats Ciulli as the name to drop.
responses.response: I take the two-part argument seriously, and I agree with you on Liu alone and on wording any B052 citation around the chemical conversion, not genome cutting. My reasons for a single part are these. The first-round record shows B007 has five supporters while B052 is preferred by two, both only as a pairing, and the 2020 CRISPR precedent is still unresolved for it. Taking Ciulli out to make room costs the part of B007 that I regard as the physical-chemistry core, the quantitative cooperativity and structure-based design. I would rather give B007 the full three-name credit than split the cap across two parts with one weaker. I do not oppose B052 as the committee's second choice.

responses.point: Somfai argues that C-N coupling is distinct from the 2010 prize because amine binding, deprotonation and avoidance of beta-hydride elimination required a different mechanistic solution, and that degraders are largely medicinal chemistry on E3 ligase biology.
responses.response: You answered the question I put to you in round 1: the reductive elimination from a palladium amide and the ligand design to suppress beta-hydride elimination are a distinct step, and I now count B029 as a strong, clean, mature candidate and rank it as my first alternative. I do not accept that degraders are only medicinal chemistry. The ternary-complex cooperativity is a quantitative, measurable principle, and it explains why a weak binder can yield efficient degradation, which a ligand-optimisation account does not. We also differ on timing. You think it better to wait; I think the principle is confirmed even if approval is pending. That is a judgment call, not something either of us can settle with evidence.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, calls the maturity concern honest, and notes that clinical status is unverified and that B052 or B029 is the fallback if clinical proof is required.
responses.response: We agree on the slate and the fallbacks. In round 1 I asked whether a later year, after an approval, would be better. I now think the cost of waiting is lower than I implied, but the argument for acting now does not depend on a clinical endpoint: a citation for the induced-proximity principle needs the ternary-complex evidence, which is already extensive. I would ask the expert report to state the late-stage trial status explicitly so that our maturity claim is checked, not assumed. If it showed that the clinical record is thin or the compounds are failing for reasons tied to the principle, I would move to B029.

responses.point: Zou pairs C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) with base editing (Liu), regards B007 as a real alternative but more crowded and less settled, and prefers cleaner attribution this year.
responses.response: I take the attribution point: B029 is cleaner than B007, and I count that for it. But I do not find B007 less settled scientifically. The ternary-complex mechanism has been reproduced across many ligases and companies, and the contested part is who sits in the third seat, not whether the effect is real. I also have a concern about pairing synthetic methodology with genome engineering, which you acknowledge as an awkward fit with no shared theme; the committee has a stronger case for a single coherent achievement than for a combination of unrelated ones.

uncertainties: The current clinical status of late-stage degraders, which I cannot verify from the materials I am permitted to read and which bears on how strongly maturity can be asserted.
Whether the committee accepts that the cereblon glue strand is a separate discovery that can be excluded from this citation, and whether it would then be proposed as its own prize later.
The exact priority split between the 2001 concept paper and the later drug-like VHL and cereblon degraders, recalled from memory.
Whether B029 should have been my preferred choice if the committee weights attribution clarity above novelty of mechanism.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited person. As a physicist I judge chemical biology outside my own field and rely on Aqvist and Aili for the medicinal chemistry. I share a Lund affiliation with Sparr and Somfai, which is not a conflict with any candidate. As chair I note that I opened with B001 and have moved away from it on the evidence in round 1. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1 and has no recusal.
